entities.summary:
Death is the end of life, a universal and irreversible cessation of biological functions that sustain a living organism. Despite its ubiquity, the moment of death remains a complex and difficult-to-define event, with some organisms, such as the immortal jellyfish, defying conventional notions of mortality.

    The identification of death has been a subject of intense philosophical, scientific, and religious inquiry throughout human history. From the earliest recorded attempts to understand the human condition to modern-day debates over the nature of consciousness and the afterlife, death has remained a profound and recurring theme in human experience.

    As a universal human experience, death has had a profound impact on the development of human societies, cultures, and belief systems. It has influenced the way we think about life, death, and the afterlife, shaping our relationships with the dead, our attitudes towards mortality, and our understanding of the meaning and purpose of human existence.

    The study of death has also been closely tied to the development of various fields of knowledge, including biology, medicine, philosophy, and theology. From the discovery of the human body to the development of modern medical practices, the study of death has played a crucial role in shaping our understanding of the human condition and the natural world.
